applies_to: Trane IntelliPak large packaged rooftop units running the Symbio 800 controller.
summary: IntelliPak rooftops with Symbio 800 controls publish about 380 BACnet objects covering supply and exhaust fans, economizer, DX compressors, heat, energy recovery and power metering. Writable objects are AV/BV/MV setpoints and BAS commands, some with a heartbeat. Power meter points only appear when the meter option is installed.
notes: Only the points that apply to the unit's factory configuration show up; the doc lists every possible point.
Name suffixes carry meaning: Status/Local/Active/Input are read-only, BAS/Command/Request/Setpoint value objects are the ones a BAS writes, and Arbitrator objects show which source is winning.
BI-11000 to BI-11999 are reserved for user-created diagnostic points made in Tracer TU; they are not listed.
The Symbio 800 integration guide (BAS-SVP083) covers BACnet IP and BACnet MS/TP; the rotary address sets the MS/TP MAC and a default Device ID of 1-127, and a software Device ID can be set instead.
The same document also maps every object to a Modbus register; only the BACnet side is listed here.

source.title: Symbio 800 Integration Points List BACnet/Modbus - IntelliPak

integration.summary: Schedule the unit with MV 10106 Occupancy Request and write the BAS setpoints you need: space, discharge air, duct static. MI 10119 Arbitration Method must read 'Full (Auto) Source' for BAS values to win over local ones. Sensor BAS points and the External setpoints AV 10183-10187 carry a 900 s heartbeat in the points list, so rewrite them periodically.

integration.enable: The integration guide describes an arbitration method: with 'full/auto' the BMS value is used ahead of local or default values, and with 'local' BMS values are ignored. MI 10119 Arbitration Method (read-only) shows which is active; the documents don't name a BACnet point to change it. BI 10211 Equipment Stop Status reports stop/auto; no BAS start/stop command is listed.
integration.heartbeat: The points list gives a 900 s heartbeat for the sensor BAS values (AV 10111, 10113-10116, 10118, 10119) and the External setpoints (AV 10183-10187). The Symbio 800 integration guide doesn't describe what happens when it expires.
integration.remote_sensors: Write BMS values to the '... BAS' AVs (AV 10114 Space Temperature BAS, AV 10113 Outdoor Air Temperature BAS, AV 10119 Space Humidity BAS, AV 10118 Space CO2 Concentration BAS, AV 10111 Discharge Air Temperature BAS). The '... Arbitrator' AVs show all sources in their priority array; the guide notes the default for sensor arbitrators is invalid, so the value must come from the BMS or a local sensor. Direct capacity/fan/damper control uses the 'Setpoint External' AVs together with their 'Setpoint Enable External' BVs (e.g. AV 10187 with BV 10131).
setup: With no protocol specified at order, the controller ships as BACnet MS/TP at 76,800 bps with the rotary address at 000, and MS/TP is disabled at 000. Set a rotary address of 001-127 to bring it online.
The rotary address sets the MS/TP MAC and the Device ID and takes effect without a power cycle. A software Device ID (1-4194302) can be set in the web UI, Tracer SC+ or Tracer TU.
The web UI is reached only over USB at http://198.80.18.1/; the Ethernet ports do not serve it.
BACnet IP uses Ethernet port 1 (or the optional USB Wi-Fi adapter); the default UDP port is 47808. Enable BBMD only if this is the only BACnet IP device on the subnet, then fill in the BDT.
MS/TP wiring lands on the P1 link; P2 and P3 are for factory devices only, and Ethernet port 2 is only for the touch-screen display.
gotchas: Communicated units (I-P or SI) are fixed at the factory; changing them in the field needs a Trane representative. Web UI display units do not change the BACnet values.
Points that don't apply to the unit's configuration are absent, and a technician can 'recycle' (remove) factory points from the interface, so a missing object may have been recycled.
BI-11000 to BI-11999 are reserved for user-created diagnostic points made in Tracer TU.
Arbitrator objects show as writable but are meant to be read; write the matching '... BAS' object instead.
